original_question: Let G be a finitely generated amenable orderable group, and φ : G → Homeo+ R an action of G without global fixed points. Is it true that φ is either semi-conjugate to an affine action or laminar?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact formulation. It has the right class of groups (finitely generated amenable orderable groups), the right dynamical setting (an action phi: G -> Homeo_+(R) with no global fixed point), and the right dichotomy (either semi-conjugate to an affine action or laminar).
missing_details: The paper states this as Question 6.4, i.e. an open problem/question, not as a theorem or established conjecture.
To make the question stand-alone, one should spell out that Homeo_+(R) means orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of R.

The nearby context explicitly defines semi-conjugacy for actions without global fixed points: two actions phi_1, phi_2 are semi-conjugate if there exists a (phi_1, phi_2)-equivariant non-decreasing map h: R -> R.

The paper’s nearby context also defines the relevant meaning of laminar on R: there exists an interval I subset R such that for any two translates g(I), h(I), they are either nested or disjoint, and the union of all translates covers R.
The phrase affine action is not expanded in the statement itself, so a stand-alone version should say that the comparison action is by orientation-preserving affine transformations of R.

The motivational paragraph comes from dynamical realizations of left-orders, which are faithful, but Question 6.4 itself does not add faithfulness as a hypothesis; a refined version should not insert it.
refined_question: Let G be a finitely generated amenable orderable group, and let phi: G -> Homeo_+(R) be an action without global fixed points. Must it be the case that either (i) phi is semi-conjugate to an action of G by orientation-preserving affine transformations of R, meaning that there exists a non-decreasing map h: R -> R intertwining the two actions, or else (ii) phi is laminar, in the sense that there exists an interval I subset R such that for every g, h in G, the intervals g(I) and h(I) are either nested or disjoint, and union over g in G of g(I) equals R?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the paper’s Question 6.4 in §6.2. The only substantive omissions are the definitions supplied in the immediately preceding context: semi-conjugacy is defined via a G-equivariant non-decreasing map R -> R, and laminarity is explained by the interval-translate condition. The opening sentence of §6.3 confirms that this is exactly the laminar notion introduced just above in Michele Triestino’s subsection. Because Question 6.4 itself does not assume faithfulness, the refined version keeps the statement at exactly that level rather than importing the faithfulness of dynamical realizations from the motivational discussion.
